And His saying: ﴿And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others﴾, its meaning: He took some of them as a close friend (khalil), spoke directly to some of them, subjected the jinn, mankind, the birds and the wind to some of them, and brought the dead to life for some of them. This is the meaning of the preference.

And His saying: ﴿And We gave David the Psalms﴾. They said: the Zabur is a book comprising one hundred and fifty surahs, all of which are glorification, exaltation and praise of Allah, and in it there is no command, no prohibition, no lawful and no unlawful. The meaning of the verse is: since you did not deny the preference of all the prophets and their being given scriptures, do not deny the preference of the Prophet and his being given the Qur'an. It is permissible that this address is directed to the People of the Book, and it is permissible that it is directed to a people among the idolaters of the Arabs who acknowledged this. The Zabur is derived from the root z-b-r, and zabr is writing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 56:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides Him﴾. It is narrated that when the polytheists were struck by famine, to the point that they ate dogs and carrion, they appealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) to pray for them. So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed﴾ to be gods ﴿besides Him﴾, meaning besides Allah.

And His saying: ﴿So they have no power to remove the harm from you﴾, meaning the removal of hunger and famine from you.

And His saying: ﴿Nor to transfer it﴾, meaning they have no power to change the condition, transferring it from sickness to health, from drought to fertility, and from hardship to ease.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those whom they call upon﴾. Ibn Mas'ud read: "Those whom you call upon" (ʾUlāʾika alladhīna tadʿūn). It is also related from him that he said: Some people among the polytheists used to worship some jinn, then the jinn who were being worshipped embraced Islam, while these people remained upon their polytheism; so God, exalted is He, revealed this verse. Its meaning: Indeed, those whom you used to call upon and worship ﴿seek means⦆ — that is, they seek, ask for — ﴿to their Lord the means (al-wasīlah)﴾. Al-wasīlah is the lofty rank in Paradise. It has also been said: al-wasīlah is everything by which one seeks a means of access to God, exalted is He, that is, draws near.

His saying: ﴿which of them is nearest﴾. Its meaning: they look to see which of them is nearest in means. It has also been said: which of them is nearest to God, so that they may seek a means through him. It has also been said: the verse refers to ʿUzayr, the Messiah, and others. It has also been said: the verse refers to the angels, for the polytheists used to worship the angels, and the angels are servants who seek a means to God; and this applies to a group of the polytheists, not to all of them.

His saying: ﴿and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾, meaning: the jinn who embraced Islam and the angels, or ʿUzayr and the Messiah.

In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is said: "If the fear and hope of the believer were weighed, they would be balanced."

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared﴾, that is, one must seek caution against it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 58:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection﴾ mean: there is no city but that We will destroy it. The destruction of the believers is by causing them to die, and the destruction of the disbelievers is by total annihilation and punishment. It is also said that His words ﴿destroy it﴾ refer to the believers, by causing them to die.

His words ﴿or punish it with a severe punishment﴾ refer to the disbelievers.

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir, with his chain of narration from Muqatil ibn Sulayman, who said: "I found in the book of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, which is the 'Stored Book' (al-kitab al-makhzun), in which he mentioned what Allah destroys the people of each town with. As for Makkah, it will be destroyed by the two Abyssinians (al-habshan). As for Madinah, by hunger. As for Basra, by division (al-farq). As for Kufa, by an enemy whom Allah has set over them. As for al-Sham and Egypt, woe to them from their enemy. It is also said: they will be ruined by winds. As for Isfahan, Fars and Kirman, by darkness and thunderbolts; likewise it is mentioned concerning Armenia and Azerbaijan. As for al-Rayy, their enemy from the Daylam will overcome them. As for Hamadhan, an enemy will destroy them, so there will be no Hamadhan after that. As for Nishapur, by thunder, lightning and wind. As for Marw, sand will overcome it, and by it there will be many scholars. As for Herat, they will be rained upon with serpents, which will devour them. As for Sistan, it will be destroyed by wind. As for Balkh, water will overcome it and it will be destroyed. As for Bukhara, the Turks will overcome them. As for Samarqand, Farghana, al-Shash, Isbijab and Khwarazm, the sons of Qantura ibn Karkara will overcome them, and they will be destroyed to the last man." The report is very strange. In some narrations: "Woe to the people of Baghdad, they will be swallowed up by the earth," and the report is strange.

In some of the musnads, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, he said: "Allah does not destroy a people until adultery and usury become widespread among them."

His words ﴿That was written in the Book as a record﴾ mean: written down. The "Book" means the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

In the well-known reports from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen, and He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will happen until the Day of Resurrection.'"

It is said: sattara means "he wrote."

"The saying of Him, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾, and so on. If someone says: How is it possible that God does not send signs because the former peoples denied them? And what is the reason for refraining from sending signs on account of the former peoples' denial? The question is well known, and it is problematic. The answer comes in two ways. The first: the "except" (illa) is elided, and a similar usage is the saying of the poet:

(Every brother who parts from his brother... by the life of your father 'Amr, except the two Farqads [i.e., the two stars]...)

Its meaning: 'And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs, even if the former peoples denied them.' That is, the denial of the former peoples does not prevent Us from sending signs.

The second answer, which is the well-known one: 'And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs that the disbelievers proposed.' For they said to the Prophet: 'Make Safa gold for us, or move these mountains away from us so that we may cultivate the lands.'

As for His saying: ﴿except that the former peoples denied them﴾, the meaning of the exception concerns the destruction of the former peoples when they denied the signs that were proposed. We have established that this community is granted respite from punishment. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Nay, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter﴾. The summary of the answer: the former peoples proposed signs, and when they were given them, they denied them and were destroyed. So if We gave these people the proposed signs and they denied them, We would hasten punishment upon them. And We have decreed their respite. The evidence for the soundness of this answer is that He said: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾, that is, a clear, luminous sign, or a sign by which the truth is seen. And His saying: ﴿but they wronged themselves through it﴾, that is, they denied it, so they were hastened with the punishment. This is what is meant, even though it is not explicitly mentioned.

And His saying: ﴿And We send the signs only as a warning﴾, that is, as a caution."

Tafsir al-Qur'an by al-Sam'ani, on Surah 17, verse 60:

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when We said to you, "Indeed your Lord has encompassed the people."﴾ Mujahid said: that is, they are in His grip. Al-Hasan said: He prevented them from killing you or from plotting against you by means other than killing. This is the meaning of ihata (encompassing).

And His words: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾ Most scholars hold that this vision is the night of the Mi'raj (Ascension). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and others.

If someone says: was the night of the Mi'raj a vision seen with the eyes, not a dream? The answer: it is authentically related from Abdullah ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding this verse: it is a vision of the eyes, which the Prophet ﷺ was taken on a night journey during that night.

﴿And the accursed tree﴾ is the tree of Zaqqum.

The Shaykh, the Imam, the Most Eminent Abu al-Muzaffar Mansur ibn Muhammad al-Sam'ani said: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i informed us in Mecca, saying: Abu al-Hasan ibn Faras informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Dayboli informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi informed us, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, (as) mentioned by al-Bukhari in his Sahih.

As for mentioning the ru'ya (dream) in the sense of ru'yah (sight) here, it is permissible, because both are derived from one meaning. Some have said: he had two ascensions: a Mi'raj of sight and a Mi'raj of dream.

As for the meaning of the trial according to this view: some people among those who believed apostatized when they heard about this from the Prophet. In the original interpretation of the verse there is another view: that the vision mentioned in the verse is that the Prophet saw in sleep that he had entered Mecca, so he hastened and set out for Mecca in the year of al-Hudaybiyah in ihram for 'Umrah. The Companions reported that he had seen this vision. When he was prevented from Mecca until he needed to return, some people were tried by that.

In the well-known report, 'Umar said to Abu Bakr: "Did he not see that he would enter Mecca?" Abu Bakr said to him: "Did he say that he would enter it this year?" He said: "No." He said: "He will enter it..." the report to its end.

A third view regarding the verse is what al-Damyati related in his tafsir from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Prophet saw in his sleep as if the sons of al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As were leaping upon his pulpit like monkeys" — and in another narration, "they were passing his pulpit back and forth like a ball" — and that displeased him. So he summoned Abu Bakr and 'Umar and informed them of that. Then he heard that al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As was relating the vision, so he did not suspect Abu Bakr, but suspected 'Umar, and summoned him and said to him: "Why did you disclose my secret?" He said: "By Allah, I did not mention it to anyone." The Messenger of Allah said: "How, when al-Hakam is relating this to the people?!" 'Umar said: "We will meet again until I inform you who spread it." He said: So he and Abu Bakr came and sat with the Messenger in that place, and they began to mention this. Then 'Umar went out hastily, and there was al-Hakam listening. He mentioned that to the Prophet, and the Messenger of Allah expelled him from Medina, and neither Abu Bakr nor 'Umar sheltered him, and he remained banished until the time of 'Uthman — the story to its end. This is the vision mentioned in the verse.

It has been narrated that the Prophet was never seen laughing fully from the time he saw this vision until he died.

As for the accursed tree, most scholars say it is the tree of Zaqqum. If it is said: where did He curse it in the Qur'an? The answer: the intended meaning of "the accursed tree" is that the one who eats it is accursed. Al-Zajjaj said: the Arabs say of every repugnant food: "accursed food." Accordingly, the verse's sense is: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you, nor the accursed tree [in the Qur'an], except as a trial for the people.﴾

As for the trial concerning the tree of Zaqqum, it is of two kinds. First: Abu Jahl said: "Fire consumes trees, and Muhammad claims that fire makes a tree grow." Second: Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ari said: "O people, Muhammad frightens us with Zaqqum, and we know Zaqqum only as butter and dates." Abu Jahl said: "O slave-girl, bring us some, so we may feed ourselves on it (tazqimuna)."

The second view regarding the tree of Zaqqum is that it is the kashuta plant, which coils around trees and dries them out. A third view: the accursed tree in the Qur'an is the sons of al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As, namely Marwan and his sons.

This was mentioned by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, but a group of exegetes denied this view. And Allah knows best.

As for His words: ﴿And We warn them﴾ that is, We warn them, ﴿but it only increases them﴾ that is, the warning only increases them ﴿in transgression, a great transgression﴾ that is, in rebellion and great arrogance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 61:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾. We have already mentioned the meaning of prostration (sujud) in Surat al-Baqarah, and the disagreement of people concerning it. And His saying: ﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis. He said, "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ Its meaning: to one whom You created from clay. And His saying: ﴿clay﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), meaning: in the state of his being clay. In the verse there is an ellipsis (hadhf), and its meaning is: "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay, while You created me from fire? Fire has a merit over clay, for fire consumes clay." The wretched one did not know that substances are all of one kind, and that merit is what God, exalted is He, bestows. Among the benefits of clay are things that equal the benefits of fire, or exceed them, and clay has a nobility of disposition that fire does not have.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that God sent Iblis until he took a handful of earth from the ground, and in it there was the brackish and the sweet. From it He created Adam. Whoever was created from the sweet was happy, even if he was born of two disbelieving parents, and whoever was created from the brackish was wretched, even if he was from the loins of (the children of Adam).

Ibn 'Abbas said: His saying, ﴿"Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ means: "Shall I submit to one whom You created from clay, when I was the one You brought?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 62:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He said: "Tell me, is this the one whom You have honored above me?"﴾ His saying "a-ra'aytaka" (arayta, "have you seen/tell me") means: inform me. The "ka" (the kaf) is for emphasizing the address to the one addressed. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿this one whom You have honored above me﴾ means: You honored him over me and preferred him.

His saying: ﴿If You give me respite﴾ means: give me time ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾. The wicked one hoped to be given respite until the Day of Resurrection and to escape death. God, Exalted is He, refused this for him, as He said in Surat al-Hijr: ﴿Indeed, you are among those given respite until a known time.﴾

His saying: ﴿I will surely seize (la-ahtanikanna) his descendants﴾. They said: I will utterly uproot them. It is said: "ihtanaka al-jarad al-zar'" (the locusts stripped the crops) when they uprooted it entirely. Some said: it is derived from "hanak al-dabbah" (the bridle of the animal), when one ties a rope to the lower jaw of the animal (rasan) with which he drives it.

Its meaning: I will drive them to sins with a driving, and I will incline them towards it with an inclination. It was said: I will gain control over them through misguidance. It was said: I will mislead them.

His saying: ﴿his descendants (dhurriyyatahu)﴾ means: his offspring ﴿except a few﴾. The few are those of whom God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them.﴾ If it is asked: how did Iblis know that most of the descendants of Adam would follow him? We say: the answer is from two aspects. First, when he saw Adam's submission to his whispering, he hoped for his descendants.

The second: he saw that written in the Preserved Tablet, and he knew it as the angels knew when they said: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Go, and whoever follows you among them, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense.﴾ That is: "muwaffaran" (complete, full). The meaning of "muwaffaran" is: "mukammalan" (perfected, complete). The poet said:

(And whoever makes goodness a thing other than his honor... it will be explained to him, and whoever does not guard himself against insult will be insulted.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 64:

The Exalted's words: ﴿And incite﴾. Al-Azhari said: its meaning is: call them with a call that stirs them to answer you, i.e., that makes them light-headed (fa-tastakhiffahum).

It was also said: "Istafziz bihim" means: hasten them (asri' bihim). It was said: drive them to misguidance (ahmilhum 'ala al-igh'a). His words: ﴿those whom you can﴾ among them: we have explained the meaning of "istita'a" (ability). The poet recited, regarding the meaning of istifza:

(So I said to her: "Be not you one who stirs ... the women of the eyes and the eloquent, the adorned.")

His words: ﴿with your voice﴾. Mujahid said: singing and frivolity. Al-Hasan said: the tambourine (duff) and the flute (mizmar). It was also said: every voice that calls to other than obedience to God. It was also said: every speech spoken about other than the Essence of God.

His words: ﴿and muster against them﴾ means: gather against them your schemes and tricks. It is said: "ajlaba 'ala al-'aduw" when one gathers an army against the enemy. In the proverb: "If you do not prevail, then muster (fa-ajlib)." It was also said its meaning is: gather against them your army and your troops.

His words: ﴿with your cavalry and your infantry﴾: every rider in disobedience is of Iblis's cavalry, and every walker in his disobedience is on Iblis's foot. Al-khayl is the rider, and al-rajl is the walkers. In a report: "O cavalry of God, mount up!"

His words: ﴿and share with them in wealth﴾: every gain from what is unlawful, and every expenditure in disobedience of God, is that in which Iblis shares. It was also said: what he made attractive to them of the bahira, the sa'iba, the wasila and the ham.

His words: ﴿and children﴾. Concerning this there are sayings. Ibn 'Abbas said: the buried alive (al-mawuda).

Mujahid said: children of fornication. Others said: it is their making them Jews, Christians and Magians.

From Ibn 'Abbas in another narration, it is: naming their children 'Abd al-'Uzza, 'Abd al-Dar, 'Abd Manaf, and what is similar to that.

In some of the musnads, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man came to him and said: "My wife woke up, and in her private part there was a flame of fire." He said: "That is from the intercourse of the jinn." He said: "Then what of their children?" He said: "These are the effeminate (al-mukhannathun)."

From Ja'far ibn Muhammad: Satan sits upon the man's penis; when he does not mention God's name, he has intercourse with his wife along with him, and he ejaculates into her private part as the man does. Something close to this is narrated from Mujahid. In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "Among you are two-sided ones (mughribun)." It was said: "And who are the mughribun?" He said: "Those with whom the jinn have shared."

His words: ﴿and promise them﴾ means: say to them, "There is no Paradise and no Fire." It was also said: say to them, "There is no resurrection."

His words: ﴿Satan promises them only delusion﴾. Al-ghurur: making falsehood appear attractive by what one supposes to be truth. In some exegeses, on the authority of Anas from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Iblis said: 'O Lord, You cursed me and expelled me from Paradise on account of Adam; so empower me over him and over his offspring.' God the Exalted said: 'You are empowered.' He said: 'I cannot do it except by You, so increase me.' He said: ﴿And incite whom you can among them﴾ up to the end of the verse. Adam said: 'O Lord, You empowered Iblis over me and over my offspring, and I cannot withstand him except by You, so what is for me?' He said: 'No child will be born to you except that I shall appoint for him those who guard him.' He said: 'Increase me.' He said: 'A good deed is multiplied tenfold, and an evil deed is recompensed by its like.' He said: 'Increase me.' He said: 'Repentance is offered as long as the soul is in the body.' He said: 'Increase me.' He said: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ to the end of the verse." In this report: "Iblis said: 'O Lord, You sent prophets and sent down books; so what is my Qur'an?' He said: 'Poetry.' He said: 'What is my book?' He said: 'Tattooing.' He said: 'What is my food?' He said: 'Every food over which the name of God has not been mentioned.' He said: 'What is my drink?' He said: 'Every intoxicant.' He said: 'What are my snares?' He said: 'Women.' He said: 'What is my call?' He said: 'The flute.' He said: 'What is my house?' He said: 'The bathhouse.' He said: 'What is my gathering place?' He said: 'The marketplace.'" The report is very strange, and God knows best.

If someone says: How does God command these things, when He says: ﴿Indeed, God does not command immorality﴾? The answer: this is a command of threat and warning, like His words: ﴿Do what you will﴾, and like a man who says to another: "Do what you wish, you will see." Such usage is frequent.

God's words, "Indeed, My servants—over them you have no authority," have already been explained. It has also been said that its meaning is: you have no authority over them to make them commit a sin from which I will not accept their repentance.

And His words, "And sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs" mean: a Guardian, or one to whom affairs are entrusted.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 66:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships through the sea﴾, meaning: He drives and propels them. The poet said:

(O rider driving his mount onward... ask the Banu Asad what this sound is.)

And His saying: ﴿for you the ship through the sea﴾, meaning: the ship upon the sea.

﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning: that you may seek of His provision.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you﴾ is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 67:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea﴾ means: hardship at sea. He singled out the sea for mention because despair is most prevalent when hardship befalls one there.

And His saying: ﴿those whom you invoke vanish, except Him﴾ means: they are lost and fall away.

And His saying: ﴿those whom you invoke﴾ means: those whom you call upon ﴿except Him﴾ means: except Allah. This has the same meaning as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him.﴾

And His saying: ﴿But when He brings you safely to land, you turn away﴾ means: turning away from sincerity and from seeking refuge in Allah.

And His saying: ﴿and man is ever ungrateful﴾ means: disbelieving.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 17, verse 68:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do you feel secure that He will not cause the earth to swallow you on the side of the land?﴾ The khasf (cave-in, swallowing) of a thing is its concealment in the earth. It is also said: it is the earth's swallowing of it.

His saying ﴿on the side of the land﴾ means: a part of the land.

His saying: ﴿Or send against you a violent wind (hasib) of pebbles﴾ means: a wind carrying pebbles, and al-hasba' (pebbles) are stones. Its meaning: a wind that pelts with stones.

Some of the lexicographers said: al-hasib is hail, and some of them said: al-hasib is snow. Al-Farazdaq said:

(Facing the north wind as it drives them, / there is a hasib like scattered cotton fluff.)

His saying: ﴿then you would find for yourselves no advocate against Us﴾ means: whom will you entrust your affairs to, so that he may save you?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 69:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Or do you feel secure that He will not return you into it another time﴾, meaning: into the sea, another time. And His statement: ﴿and send against you a violent wind, and drown you for your disbelief﴾. Al-qasif (the violent one): it is the wind that breaks everything it reaches.

And His statement: ﴿and drown you for your disbelief﴾, meaning: because of your disbelief.

And His statement: ﴿then you will not find for yourselves any avenger against Us for it﴾, meaning: a tha'ir (one seeking vengeance), and he is the seeker of revenge; thus said al-Farra'. It was said: one who will pursue us with denial.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And We have honoured the children of Adam﴾. There are several views on this. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: it is their eating with the hand, whereas the rest of the animals eat with their mouths. It was also said: it is the uprightness and erectness of their stature, while beasts are bent down over their faces. It was said: it is by intellect and discernment. It was said: it is that all things were subjected to them. It was said: it is that the best nation brought forth for mankind was made among them. It was said: it is by writing and the pen.

His saying: ﴿And We carried them on land and sea﴾, that is, We carried them on land upon beasts, and on the sea upon ships.

His saying: ﴿and provided them with good things﴾. The good things that God the Exalted provided for the children of Adam in this world are known. It was said: they are the lawful. And it was said.

﴿And We have preferred them above many of those We have created, with a [marked] preference﴾. Abu al-Nadr Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi said: above all creation, except a group of the angels, among them Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil and 'Azra'il. Regarding the preference of humans over angels, or of angels over humans, there is much discussion, which is not the place for it. The apparent meaning of the verse is that He preferred them over many of His creatures, not over all of them. It is permissible to mention the majority while meaning the whole. The more correct view is that humanity is superior to the angels with a known detail: the common righteous believers are superior to the common angels, and the elite believers are superior to the elite angels. God the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, they are the best of creation﴾, and "al-bariyyah" (creation) refers to everything God has created in general.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 71:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day when We shall summon every people with their leader﴾. There are several opinions regarding this. The first: with their prophet. The second: with their book. The third: with their deeds. And it is reported from Ibn 'Abbas: a leader of guidance and a leader of misguidance. And it is reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: every people will gather around their leader in good and in evil. And in a report: On the Day of Resurrection it will be called out: "Stand up, O followers of Musa! O followers of 'Isa! O followers of Muhammad (ﷺ)! O followers of Shaytan! O followers of so-and-so!"

And in the Jami' of Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi, concerning this verse: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The believer will be given his book in his right hand, his body will be stretched to sixty cubits, his face will be made bright, and a crown of pearls will be placed upon his head. He will come to his companions and say to them: 'Rejoice, for each of you will have the like of this.' As for the disbeliever, he will be given his book in his left hand, his body will be stretched to sixty cubits, his face will be made black, and a crown of fire will be placed upon his head. He will come to his companions and say to them: 'Rejoice, for each of you will have the like of this.'"

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Then whoever is given his book in his right hand, those will read their book﴾. And "the book" is the record of good deeds and evil deeds.

His statement: ﴿And they will not be wronged a fibre﴾, that is: nothing will be reduced from their due by the amount of a fibre.

And the fatil (fibre) is that which is in the split of a date-stone. It was also said: it is what is twisted between the fingers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 72:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way﴾. The blindness here is not blindness of sight, because people will be resurrected with the most perfect creation, bodies made sound for eternal abiding. In a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "You will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised (ghurlan)," and his words "bihima" (with them) mean: bodies made sound for eternity. Based on this, the meaning of His words ﴿And whoever is blind in this﴾ is: blind of heart to seeing [the truth], ﴿then he will be blind in the Hereafter﴾, that is, more blind.

It was also said that its meaning is: whoever was far from the truth in this world will be even farther in the Hereafter. And it was said: whoever was blinder to reflection (i'tibar) in this world will be blinder in the Hereafter to excuse-making (i'tidhar).

As for His words ﴿and further astray from the way﴾, that is, more mistaken in the path.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you﴾. Its meaning: they would turn you away from that which We revealed to you. The occasion of revelation of the verse was that the polytheists said to the Prophet: "Drive these poor men away from you so that we may sit with you and become Muslims." He was inclined to do so, and then they would call them back later. So Allah, may He be exalted, sent down this verse. It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid that they both said: They asked the Prophet to touch their gods (with a gesture of respect), so that they would embrace Islam and follow him. The Prophet said within himself: "What harm is there in my doing that, since Allah knows that I dislike it?" This was a passing thought of the heart and not a firm resolve. So Allah, may He be exalted, sent down this verse. The third opinion: the people of Ta'if came to the Prophet wishing to embrace Islam. He had found their affair difficult, and he had besieged them for about ten nights without conquering them. When they came, they said to the Prophet: "We will become Muslims on condition that we do not bow (in prayer), and that you let us enjoy al-Lat for a year without worshipping it," and they mentioned other things besides this. He said: "As for abandoning bowing, there is no good in a religion that has no bowing in it. As for al-Lat, I will not leave an idol among the Muslims." They pressed him again concerning the matter of al-Lat, saying: "Let the Arabs speak of the increase in our honour before you." The Prophet fell silent, and the people grew hopeful because of his silence. So Allah, may He be exalted, sent down this verse. This is a well-known opinion.

His saying: ﴿So that you would fabricate against Us other than it﴾, i.e., you would say about Us other than what We have sent down to you. His saying: ﴿And then they would have taken you as a close friend﴾, i.e., a companion and intimate friend.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 74:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined to them a little﴾. The meaning of "kāda" (almost, nearly) is: it came close, and "kidta" (you almost) means: you came close to the act.

And His words: ﴿a little﴾ are in the place of the verbal noun (maṣdar), as if He had said: "You would almost have inclined to them with some inclination." If it is said: The Prophet was protected (ma'sum, free from sin) from shirk (polytheism) and the major sins, so how is it permissible for him to come close to what they asked of him, when what they asked of him was disbelief?

The answer is in two respects. The first: we hold that the Messenger was protected from shirk and the major sins, and we interpret that what occurred from him was a passing thought (hamm) without resolve. The Prophet said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not speak it or act upon it." In sum, Allah knows His Messenger better than anyone else. Qatadah said: When this occurred, the Messenger of Allah would say after that: "O Allah, do not entrust me to myself even for the blink of an eye."

The second answer: He said: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined﴾, and He did make him firm, so he did not incline. This is like His words, the Exalted: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ up to His words: ﴿except a few﴾. Allah did show grace and mercy, and they did not follow Satan.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 75:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We not strengthened you, you would almost have inclined toward them a little.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Double the punishment of life, and double the punishment of death."

It was also said: "Double the punishment of this world, and double the punishment of the Hereafter." It was also said: "The word ḍi'f (doubling) carries the meaning of punishment, so it is as if He said: 'We would have made you taste the punishment of life and the punishment of death.' The punishment is called ḍi'f only because pain is doubled within it."

If it is asked: "Why is the punishment doubled for him?" We say: "Because of the elevation of his rank, just as the reward is doubled for him upon obedience." Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her twofold.﴾ The meaning is what we have explained.

As for His saying: ﴿Then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper.﴾ That is: you would not find anyone to prevent Our punishment from you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 76:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed they were about to unsettle you from the land to expel you from it﴾. Al-istifzaz (unsettling, provoking) is driving someone out quickly by agitation. The scholars differed concerning the meaning of this verse. Some of them said: It was revealed in Medina, and the occasion of its revelation was that the Jews of Qurayzah, al-Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa' came to the Prophet and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, you know that the lands of the prophets are Syria, and it is the holy land. When did you ever hear of a prophet from Tihamah? So come out with us to Syria; we will believe in you and support you." The Prophet resolved to leave with them and pitched his tent three miles from Medina in order to depart. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse. Here "the land" means Medina, and this is a well-known opinion.

It is related from Qatadah that he said: The verse is Meccan, and the meaning of "the land" is the land of Mecca. The polytheists had intended to expel him from it or to kill him, so Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to emigrate and to leave of his own accord.

It was also said: "The land" is the whole earth, and expulsion from it is killing.

As for His saying: ﴿And then they would not remain after you except for a little﴾. It is also recited as "khilafak" (after you), and its meaning is: after you. ﴿Except for a little﴾. The meaning of "a little" according to the second opinion is the period between the Messenger of Allah's departure and their being killed at Badr; and according to the first opinion, it is the duration of life.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 77:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A practice (sunnah) [We applied] to those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾, and the rest of the verse. The word "sunnah" is in the accusative (intasabat al-sunnah) because its meaning is: "This is the practice like the practice of those whom We sent," then the kaf (the particle of comparison, "like") was deleted, so "sunnah" became accusative. The meaning of the practice of God is the uprooting of the people by destruction when they expel the Messenger or kill him.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and you will not find any alteration in Our practice﴾, meaning: any change (tabdil). It was also said: "to Our custom," and its meaning is: what God, exalted is He, has established as custom in His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 78:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾. The scholars differed concerning "dulūk" (decline). Ibn Mas'ud said: it is the sunset (ghurūb). Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the zawal (the sun passing its zenith and beginning to decline). Both opinions have been related from them, and the Successors (tabi'un) likewise differed on this. The root meaning of dulūk is inclination (mayl), and the sun inclines when it passes its zenith or when it sets. It was also said that it derives from dalk (rubbing), since a person at zawal rubs his eyes because of the intensity of the sunlight, and rubs his eyes at sunset, so that the sun is seen clearly to know its body. The poet said:

(Lamps that are not those which are led by stars, nor those that set, the winding ones.)

The Arabs say: "a road dawālik" when it has many branches. The more preferable of the two opinions is that it be understood as zawal, because most of the Successors held this view, and because if we understand it this way, the verse encompasses all five daily prayers, for His saying ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾ includes Zuhr and 'Asr.

And His saying ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾ includes Maghrib and 'Isha'.

The darkness of the night (ghasaq al-layl) is the appearance of its darkness; it was also said: the gathering of its blackness.

And His saying ﴿and the recitation of dawn﴾, i.e., the prayer of dawn (Fajr). The scholars derived from this the obligation of recitation in the prayer, since He named the prayer "recitation" (Qur'an). And His saying ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾, i.e., it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. The meaning of "witnessed" is "attended."

It has been authentically reported through the narration of al-A'mash, may Allah have mercy on him, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning this verse: "Indeed, the recitation of dawn—the prayer of dawn—is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day." It was also said that the meaning of His saying ﴿witnessed﴾ is: people are commanded to attend it so that they may pray it in congregation. The correct view is the first opinion.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 79:**

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And during the night, perform tahajjud with it﴾. It is said: tahajjud (voluntary night prayer after sleep) means that he arose after sleep for prayer, and hajada means that he slept. Al-Azhari said: at-tahajjud is casting off the hujur (sleep), and it is sleep. It is reported from ‘Alqamah, al-Aswad and others that tahajjud occurs only after sleep.

And His words: ﴿as an additional (nafilah) for you﴾, meaning: an increase for you. It has been said: it is an increase for everyone, so what is the meaning of specifying the Prophet with this? We say: because for others it is expiation of sins, while for him it is an increase, since his sins are already forgiven. It has also been said: nafilah for you means obligatory upon you, and standing in the night was obligatory upon him. It has also been said: nafilah for you means a virtue for you, and he was singled out for mention so that he would have precedence in this virtue, and so that people would follow him in it.

And His words: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾. The exegetes have unanimously agreed that this is the station of intercession (shafa'ah), and this has been established from the Prophet. In a report from Abu Hurayrah, the Prophet recited His words: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ and said: "It is the station in which I will intercede for my community." It is also related that peace and blessings be upon him said: "I am the master of the prophets when they are raised, I am their delegate when they speak, I am their bearer of good news when they are despairing, and I am their imam when they prostrate; I speak and let it be heard, I intercede and my intercession is accepted, and I ask and I am given."

It is reported from Mujahid that he said: He will seat him upon the Throne. Others said: He will seat him upon the Kursi before Him. Some of them said: He will stand him at the right side of the Throne.

It is reported from Hudhayfah that he said: Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection in one level plain, the caller will make them hear, and the sight will penetrate them, while they are barefoot, naked and standing, and no sound will be heard from them. Then Allah, exalted is He, will say: "O Muhammad!" He will say: "At Your service and at Your pleasure, and goodness is in Your hands, and whoever is guided is one whom You have guided. Blessed and exalted are You; there is no refuge and no escape from You except to You, and I am Your servant before You." He said: "This is the praiseworthy station."

It is related from some of them that the praiseworthy station is the banner of praise that is given to the Prophet. And it is established from the Prophet that he said: "My intercession is for the people of the major sins from my community." And he said: "Every prophet has an answered supplication, and I have saved my supplication as an intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection." And from him, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: "I will not cease to intercede until documents bearing the names of people for whom the Fire has been decreed are handed to me, and until Malik, the keeper of the Fire, says: 'You have left the Fire no retribution against your community.'" The reports concerning intercession are numerous, and the first to deny it was 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd, and he is astray and an innovator, by the consensus of the People of the Sunnah.

The Exalted said: ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit."﴾ Concerning this there are several opinions. The first: "Cause me to enter Madinah with a sound entrance, and to exit Makkah with a sound exit." The mention of "sound" (ṣidq) here praises the exit, as in His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sound standing (qadam ṣidq) with their Lord﴾. So ṣidq praises the standing (qadam), and likewise His saying: ﴿In a sound seat (maq'ad ṣidq)﴾ praises the seat. It is only praise for what the exit and entrance lead to: victory, honour and the dominion of the religion.

The second opinion: "Cause me to exit Makkah and cause me to enter Makkah." This was said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk. The third opinion: "Cause me to enter into the religion and cause me to exit from this world." The fourth opinion: "Cause me to enter into the message and cause me to exit from this world, having fulfilled what was obligatory upon me concerning its rights." The fifth opinion: "Cause me to exit from the prohibitions (manāhī) and cause me to enter into the commands (awāmir)."

The two first opinions are the most well known. Al-makhraj has the meaning of the act of exiting, and al-madkhal has the meaning of the act of entering.

As for His saying: ﴿And grant me from Yourself a helping authority (sulṭān naṣīrā)﴾, Mujāhid said: "a clear proof (ḥujjah bayyinah)." Others said: "a mighty kingdom (mulkan ʿazīzan)." A mighty kingdom is one that is supported with power and proof.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 81:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And say: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish.﴾ Qatadah said: "The truth (al-haqq) is the Qur'an, and the falsehood (al-batil) is Satan." It was also said: "The truth is the worship of Allah, and the falsehood is the worship of idols."

It is established by the narration of Ibn Mas'ud that the Prophet entered Makkah while there were three hundred and sixty idols around the Ka'bah, and he began striking them and saying: "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed, falsehood was ever bound to vanish." This was related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih.

The Shaykh, the Imam, the most eminent ascetic Abu al-Muzaffar Mansur ibn Muhammad al-Sam'ani said: We were informed of it by al-Makki ibn Abd al-Razzaq al-Kushmihani, who said: My grandfather Abu al-Haytham informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firabri informed us, saying: al-Bukhari informed us, saying: Ali ibn al-Madini informed us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, the report.

In some tafsir works: the Prophet would point with his hand at the idol, and the idol would fall on its back without his touching it.

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, falsehood was ever bound to vanish﴾, i.e., going away (dhahiban). It is said: "His soul departed (zahaqat nafsuhu)" when it came out.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 82:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy﴾ to the end of the verse. It has been said that "min" (from) here is for specification of the kind (li-l-tajnis), not for partitioning (li-l-tab'id). Its meaning is: "And We send down the Qur'an, of which there is healing." It has also been said: "And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy," meaning: all of it is healing, so the part is intended as the whole, as the poet said:

(Or some souls' doves are seized by death...) meaning: all souls. Al-hamam (the doves) is death.

As for what is meant by healing, it is healing from ignorance through knowledge, from misguidance through guidance, and from doubt through certainty. It has also been said that what is meant by healing is healing from illness through seeking blessing (tabarruk) by it. And it has been said that the meaning of healing is the manifestation, through it, of the proof of the prophethood by its inimitability (i'jaz) and the wondrous arrangement and composition.

His words: ﴿and a mercy for the believers﴾, meaning: it is a blessing, an exposition, and a guidance for the believers.

His words: ﴿and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾. The meaning of the increase in loss through the Qur'an for the wrongdoers is what renewed in them of denial each time a verse was revealed, one verse after another; that is the increase in loss and disbelief.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 83:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when We bestow favour upon man﴾, meaning: with health, abundance of provision, a good life, and what is similar to that.

And His saying: ﴿he turns away﴾, meaning: he turns his back (tawalla). And His saying: ﴿and withdraws his side﴾, meaning: he keeps his side far away (tabā'ada bi-janbihi). It has been recited as "wa-nā' bi-janbihi" (and he leans away with his side), and this is close in meaning to the first. The meaning of the verse is: the manifestation of humility and sincerity in supplication and in seeking refuge with Allah at the time of trial and hardship, and abandoning that at the time of blessing and health. The meaning of withdrawing is: abandoning drawing near to Allah, and what he used to show of that at the time of harm and hardship.

And His saying: ﴿and when evil touches him, he is despairing﴾, meaning: he is in despair (āsi). Its meaning is that he humbles himself and supplicates at the time of harm and hardship, and when the answer is delayed, he despairs. It is not fitting for the believer to despair of the answer from Allah, even if the answer is delayed for a long time.

It is related from one of the Successors (tābi'ūn) that he said: "I have been supplicating Allah with one supplication for twenty years, and He has not answered me in it, yet I have not despaired of it." It was asked: "And what is that supplication?" He said: "Leaving what does not concern me."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 84:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Each acts according to his own manner (shakilatihi)﴾, meaning: according to his disposition (jadilatihi) and his nature. Its meaning is: that which resembles his creation. Some transmitters have written it as "kullun ya'mal 'ala jadilatihi" (each acts according to his jadila), which is a textual corruption (tashif) close in meaning, and corruption (tashif) in tafsir is a matter [to be avoided].

And His saying: ﴿Your Lord knows best who is best guided in the way﴾, meaning: who is clearer in path and more evident in course.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 17, verse 85:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little.﴾ ʿAlqamah related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah in a field of crops, and he was leaning on a palm-frond stalk (ʿasīb). A group of the Jews came to him and asked him about the soul. The Messenger of Allah stopped and looked toward the sky, so I knew that revelation was coming to him, and I withdrew from him. Then he said: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little.﴾" And this is a sound report.

And from Ibn ʿAbbas, through the transmission of ʿAṭāʾ: "The Quraysh gathered and said: 'Muhammad grew up among us in trustworthiness and truthfulness, and we have never accused him of lying, but he has made the claim he has made. So send a party to the Jews and ask them about him.' So they sent a group to Madinah to ask the Jews of Madinah about him. They went and asked them, and the Jews said: 'Ask him about three things. If he answers two and does not answer the third, he is a prophet; and if he answers all three, or fails to answer any of the three, he is not a prophet. Ask him about Dhu al-Qarnayn, about a group of youths who disappeared in ancient times, and about the soul'—and by 'the one he will not answer about' they meant the soul. So they returned and asked the Prophet about that, while the Quraysh were gathered, and he said: 'I will answer you tomorrow.' He did not say, 'If Allah wills.' So the revelation was delayed for forty days, as Allah the Exalted willed. Then after forty days there was revealed the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And never say of anything, 'Indeed I will do that tomorrow,' except [with the phrase], 'If Allah wills.'﴾ And revelation came concerning the story of the People of the Cave and the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, and concerning the soul there was revealed the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord.﴾"

The scholars differed concerning the soul, giving several opinions. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is Jibril, peace be upon him, and he also said in another place: ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down.﴾ It is also related from him that he said: "A creation in the heavens, from the [category of] ﴿the soul, say: the soul is by the command of my Lord﴾, the kind of the children of Adam; they have hands and feet, and they are not of the angels." Abu Salih also mentioned this. And it is related from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The soul is an angel with seventy thousand faces, for each face seventy thousand tongues"—and in another report, "seventy tongues, glorifying Allah with all of them."

And from al-Hasan al-Basri: the soul here is the Qur'an. It was also said: it is ʿIsa, peace be upon him. Its meaning is that he is neither as the Jews said nor as the Christians said, but he is the spirit of Allah and His word, which came to be by His command.

The most correct of the opinions is that the soul here is the spirit by which a person lives, and this is the view of most of the exegetes. They differed concerning it: some said it is the blood, for you see that when a person dies nothing leaves him except the blood; some said it is the breath of a person from the air, for you see that the one who is strangled dies because the breath is held back from him; some said it is an accident (ʿaraḍ); and some of them said it is a subtle body resembling wind, flowing through the hollows of the person. Whoever holds that it is a body argues from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Rather, they are alive with their Lord, provided for, rejoicing in what Allah has given them﴾, and the provision of bodies is what is conceivable, not the provision of accidents; and this is indicated by the Prophet's saying: "The souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that graze on the fruits of Paradise," or "that eat."

It is related from the Prophet that he said: "Allah the Exalted created the souls before the bodies by four thousand years." All this is evidence that the soul is a body and not an accident, and this is the better of the two views.

Some people of the meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) mentioned that the soul is a meaning in which light, goodness, knowledge, elevation and permanence are gathered. Do you not see that when it is present the eye sees and the ear hears, and when the soul departs, hearing and sight are gone? And when it is present the person is good, but when it departs he stinks; and when it is present knowledge of things is found in the person, but when it is gone he becomes ignorant; likewise life is found in him, and when it is gone the person becomes dead; and elevation and subtlety are found in him, and when it is gone he sinks and becomes base.

The most preferable of the opinions about the soul is to leave its knowledge to Allah.

It is also said: it is a meaning by which a person lives, which no one knows except Allah. The Qur'an mentions that Allah the Exalted has not informed anyone of the meaning of the soul, and no one else knows it. It is related from ʿAbd Allah ibn Buraydah that he said: "Allah the Exalted did not make any brought-near angel, nor any sent prophet, aware of the meaning of the soul, and the Messenger of Allah left this world without knowing the meaning of the soul. And Allah knows best."

As for His saying: ﴿Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord﴾, its meaning is: it is from the knowledge of my Lord. Some have said: the Messenger of Allah did know the meaning of the soul, but he did not tell them, because his leaving off informing them of it was itself a sign of his prophethood. Also, he did not inform them of it, lest his informing them become a pretext for their asking about what does not concern them.

As for His saying: ﴿and you have not been given of knowledge except a little﴾, it means: in comparison with the knowledge of Allah. It is also said that this is an address to the Jews, in the sense that He told the Prophet: "Say to the Jews." 

It was also said that it is an address to the Messenger. It is related that the Jews said: "We have been given the Torah, and in it is much knowledge." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord...﴾ the verse, meaning that what you have been given of knowledge, which is in the Torah, is little in comparison with the knowledge of Allah.
